IconFlow emotes · 55 reactions · public domain

Emotes that are still themselves at 22 pixels.

Chat draws an emote at 22 to 28 pixels, on white and on dark, from the file you uploaded. So this set was drawn for those pixels: every face sits on the rounded-square card IconFlow ships as an app icon, every line is thick enough to survive, and no two members read as the same reaction.

Twitch pack 28 · 56 · 112 px · 468 KB Discord & Slack pack 128 px · 285 KB SVG sources 31 KB

CC0: use them anywhere, change them, sell what you make. No credit needed.

The set

Shown as platforms show them: each image is the 128-pixel upload, scaled down by your browser. The small pair under each one is 22 and 28 pixels on light and dark chat.

Proven as a family

One family. No twins.

A set has to pass two tests that pull in opposite directions: its members must look related, and no two may be the same reaction at chat size. iconflow family measures both. It finds the card 34 members share from their 16-pixel fields alone — every face, and the ok hand and the check mark drawn on the same card — sets it aside, and compares what is left. The closest siblings are eye roll / nerd at 0.39, pleading / flushed at 0.43, against a floor of 0.33.

The first draft's wink was the smile with one eye closed. It came back at 0.31 — a twin — and at 22 pixels it was: one eye is two pixels. The wink you see squeezes its eye shut and opens its grin.

Make your own

Same checks, your emotes.

The packs above come out of the same build target anyone can run. Draw on the 1024 grid, then let IconFlow write every platform size, refuse a file over its upload limit, and tell you which of your emotes are twins.

The emote target and iconflow family are newer than the release on PyPI (0.5.0). Until the next release, install IconFlow from GitHub as shown.

pip install "git+https://github.com/snowyukitty/ai-iconflow"
iconflow setup
iconflow build my-emote.svg --targets emote --out out
iconflow family "emotes/*.svg" --sheet family.png
IconFlowOne master. Every surface.

The IconFlow emotes are public domain (CC0 1.0). The IconFlow name and mark are not.
